inputs.original_text: Calling this “chaos” obscures what happened: a huge “No Kings” protest was met with tear gas and arrests by federal officers, with at least 13 arrests confirmed in Portland and Denver. Branding demonstrators “agitators” is a familiar way to delegitimize dissent and shield state power from scrutiny. When people protesting face intimidation and arrest while the state commands force, that is a serious threat to democratic rights. Protecting those rights means safeguarding protest, not suppressing it.
inputs.modified_text: Calling the “No Kings” protest “chaos” shifts attention away from the state’s response: federal officers used tear gas and made arrests, with at least 13 confirmed in Portland and Denver. Dismissing demonstrators as “agitators” is a familiar tactic for making dissent seem illegitimate while shielding official force from scrutiny. When people challenging power face intimidation and arrest, the consequences fall on everyone’s right to protest. Democracy requires protecting dissent, not suppressing it.
